# How to make stickman videos with AI: viral survival reels drawn in code

**Turn a topic into a viral stickman reel: a jointed figure drawn in code, rules that appear one at a time, a two-choice ending and a 4-credit voice.**

**Price:** free on the main route, with no API key. Optional paid steps on the varg API: `video-sound` (~$0.01–0.02 per voice line, $0.01–0.06 per sound effect, $0.05 per 20 s music bed; mixing free).

**Short answer:** start with [`stickman-video`](../../stickman-video/README.md): the format, the script with word counts, the jointed rig, the build in HyperFrames and the checks. The other 4 skills below add the steps around it. Ask your agent for the result in your own words; it asks the few choices that matter before anything is paid for and hands back the files.

```bash
# Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode and other agents
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill stickman-video --skill video-script --skill video-sound --skill caption-styles --skill media-judge
```

Then ask your agent in plain words, for example: *"Make a 20-second stickman survival reel, 9:16: Day 1, you're the night guard at an empty aquarium, three rules, a choice at the end. Show me the script and six frames before the voice and the render."*

## What you need

- The generation steps call the [varg API](https://varg.ai) (Seedance, Kling, Veo, GPT Image, ElevenLabs and more on one key). Sign in to the varg MCP with OAuth or set `VARG_API_KEY`. Models are billed at provider price, 1 credit = $0.01, and the agent shows an estimate before anything expensive.
- `video-sound`: ~$0.01–0.02 per voice line, $0.01–0.06 per sound effect, $0.05 per 20 s music bed; mixing free.
- Any agent that reads Agent Skills: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode and others ([install options](../../README.md#install)).

## FAQ

### Is there a free AI stickman video generator?

Yes. stickman-video draws and animates the figures in code and renders on your machine for free; only a narrator voice is a paid call (4 credits, $0.04, for 60 words on varg), and your own recording costs nothing. kaomei/stickman-video-director is a free MIT skill for clip prompts or its own local renderer.

### Why do my stick figures look stiff?

They move one joint at a time and hold poses too long. Use fixed bones posed by joint angles, two-bone legs with planted feet, a wind-up before each big move, breathing and blinks, and give the figure a new action at least every 2.5 seconds. The stickman-video rig does all of this.

### Claude Code or Codex?

Both work. The code route needs no image or video model, so any agent that can write HTML and run a command can build it. Codex users who want generated stills often use its built-in image model.

### Can a video model like Kling or Seedance make stickman videos?

It can make a painted 2.5D look, but video models drift on thin limbs: arms multiply, heads detach, two shots rarely match. Keep generated video for backgrounds or one hero shot and keep the acting figure in code.

### What makes a stickman reel travel?

A second-person situation in the first second, a DAY counter that promises a series, three or four rules that appear one at a time, a rule tested on screen, and a two-choice ending that asks for a comment.
